text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a development practice where team members regularly merge their code changes into a shared repository. Instead of waiting until the end of a project, these changes are checked automatically. A CI pipeline handles this process: it performs automated builds to compile the code and then runs a suite of tests. This approach is highly effective at catching issues early, often within minutes of a change being made. By identifying bugs or integration problems quickly, developers can fix them immediately when they are smaller and simpler to solve. This leads to higher-quality software and a smoother, more efficient workflow for the whole team.
